#radhekrishna
How to Prepare for the Amazon SDE-1 Interview

I am receiving a lot of messages on different platforms regarding Amazon interview preparation for SDE-1. So thought to make a post on it.
For SDE-1, they mainly focus on DSA and Leadership Principles, but some candidates have also been asked about OS and system design.
Yesterday only, someone told me that the second round was a system design round, even for an SDE 1 role.


1) For DSA:
Try to solve questions from the following two sheets. First, focus on Dynamic Programming (DP), Graphs, and Trees, and then move on to other topics.
i) Striver SDE Sheet
Link: https://lnkd.in/gmUr2Frg 
ii) NeetCode 150
LinkedIn: https://lnkd.in/gT8yrFbS 
Try to understand the logic and patterns behind each question. Don’t just submit solutions and move to next question.

2) For Leadership Principles:
Go through my previous post. I’ve received messages from others who were asked the same questions that I’ve listed. (See image below, she got offer from Amazon few days back).
Link: https://lnkd.in/gQetA_yh 

3) Prepare for basic Operating System questions.
4) Prepare the basic concepts of Low-Level Design (LLD) and High-Level Design (HLD).

Also, go through recent interview experiences on LeetCode for the role you are interviewing for or have an online assessment (OA). This will be really helpful because it will give you a good idea of what topics you need to prepare.

You can go through my Amazon interview experience to get some idea.
Link: https://lnkd.in/gq-nwfk3 

Amazon is hiring a lot. I know 4-5 people in my direct contact who recently received offers from Amazon, and some are still in the interview phase.

Keep coding, keep applying, and keep believing in Krishna!

#softwareengineering #experience #linkedin #amazon #interview

ai_analysis.summary: The post provides a high-level Amazon SDE-1 preparation checklist rather than substantive technical material. It recommends practicing data structures and algorithms, prioritizing dynamic programming, graphs, and trees; reviewing Leadership Principles; learning basic operating systems, low-level design, high-level design, and system design; and checking recent experiences on LeetCode. It supplies resource links but does not explain the underlying concepts or provide worked answers.
